prompt:
Implement the unfinished `vsandp/client.go` as a dependency-free Go client for the four VCF 9.1 vSAN Data Protection operations pinned in `docs/contract.json`; the specification the contract was derived from is recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`. Keep the implementation in that one file and preserve the exported API already declared there. The protected test files already declare some package-level identifiers, such as `sessionHeader`, so pick different names for anything unexported you add.

Authentication follows the contract's only security scheme, the `vmware-api-session-id` header. `Config.BootstrapToken` is a long-lived operator token that is presented to `Snapservice.Sessions_create` and to nothing else; that operation returns a short-lived working session token which every other operation must carry. Never send an `Authorization` header. Mint the first working token lazily, on the first request that needs one.

`SnapshotProtectionGroups` lists the cluster's protection groups with `Snapservice.Clusters.ProtectionGroups_list`, then for each returned group starts a one-time snapshot with `Snapservice.Clusters.ProtectionGroups.Snapshots_create$Task` and polls `Snapservice.Tasks_get` until that task reports `SUCCEEDED` or `FAILED` before moving to the next group. Return one `Result` per group in the order the list response returned them. A `FAILED` task is reported in the `BatchReport`, not returned as an error; a transport failure, a malformed response, or any other non-2xx status aborts the batch with an error.

A working token expires part way through a batch and the appliance then answers `401` with a `Vapi.Std.Errors.Unauthenticated` body. Recover without losing work: mint one replacement token and replay only the rejected request, byte for byte, then carry on where the batch left off. A rejected request never reached the appliance, so nothing that already succeeded may be repeated and no protection group may be snapshotted twice. Give up with an error if the replay is rejected as well, rather than refreshing again. A `Client` is shared by concurrent batches, so one expiry must cost one `Snapservice.Sessions_create` no matter how many in-flight requests it rejected: a caller whose token was already replaced by another goroutine reuses the new token instead of minting its own. `SessionCreates` reports the running total, including the first token.

Match the wire shape the contract describes. Send `Accept: application/json` on every request. A request with no body sends no body and no `Content-Type`; the snapshot create sends `Content-Type: application/json`. The snapshot create is only exposed as a task, so its query string is exactly `vmw-task=true`. `names` is a `form`/`explode` query parameter and is sent once per name in caller order. An unset optional field is omitted entirely and never sent empty: with no name filter the list request has no query string at all, and with no retention the request body is exactly `{"name":"..."}` rather than carrying a null or zero-valued `retention`. Serialize `CreateSpec` properties in the order the contract declares them, `name` then `retention`, and send both `RetentionPeriod` properties whenever retention is set. Percent-encode identifiers interpolated into paths.

Reject bad input before any request goes out: a missing base URL or bootstrap token, a missing cluster or snapshot name, an empty or repeated entry in the name filter, and a retention without a unit or without a positive duration.

The in-memory mock in `vsandp/mock_test.go` serves only the operations the contract names and logs every request for the wire-level assertions in `vsandp/wire_test.go`; verification never contacts a live VMware endpoint or opens a network socket. Run `bash protected_tests/verify.sh` to check the implementation.
